items.title: Richard Brunies Interview, 1959-04-27
items.q: Buck Rogers. And drum. Buck Rogers. Me on trumpet.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. When did you give up music? How long since you played music? I thought about 20 years ago. 25 years. 25 years. 25 years. You have a better memory than any of us. Well, it was a happy day in my life. Oh, who tell it? Did you ever have your own band that you were the leader that just played with other bands?

Well, you had the band when you was out in Bucktown. It was your band. Oh, I took it. I was Jesus in the band. Yeah, but I mean, it was still your band. East End. East End. East End. East End. Uncle Lemon. Didn't like the name of Bucktown, so they had a change. No. East End. East End. East End. East End. East End. East End. Violin. Not me. Violin, the piano. Buck Rogers. And drum. Buck Rogers. Me on trumpet. And a banjo player. And it wasn't that far from the roof garden. And that roof garden band was…
Who was playing over at the roof garden? Uh, what's his name? You like?
